findings.evidence: The proof invokes the mean value theorem to deduce strict monotonicity, but that theorem requires continuity on each closed subinterval. The stated sine and cosine derivative result supplies differentiability only; this item's dependencies and Facts do not supply continuity. The local result cor-differentiable-implies-continuous would close the gap if added and cited, or continuity could be proved directly.

The endpoint values and monotonicity do not establish that sine and cosine attain every intermediate value. Step 2.1 needs continuity and the intermediate value theorem to conclude that both ranges are exactly [-1,1]; neither is cited there or included in this item's dependencies. The local thm-intermediate-value, together with continuity of sine and cosine, supplies a direct repair.

The base assertion at n=1 for U_n requires sin(2θ)=2sin(θ)cos(θ), and the induction step appeals to the cosine and sine second-order recurrences without stating or deriving them. The addition formula is listed in deps, but the proof has no corresponding Fact or exact citation and gives only “the usual” recurrences. Writing the base computations and deriving the recurrences from the addition formulas would close these short gaps.

Step 1.1 uses Heine–Cantor on [0,1] without establishing compactness of this domain, then chooses M with |f|≤M although [L1] supplies only uniform continuity. The cited result does not supply either the compactness of [0,1] or boundedness of f. Applying the local Heine–Borel/extreme-value theorem to the nonempty closed bounded interval [0,1] would supply both prerequisites.

The proof defines g(t)=f(a+(b-a)t) and immediately applies the unit-interval Weierstrass result. That result requires g to be continuous, but continuity of this affine composition is not established or cited. An explicit continuity check for the affine map followed by the local composition-of-continuous-functions theorem would close the gap.

The small-r case is concluded by quantifying over rational ε only. The definition of sequence convergence quantifies over every positive real ε; noting that each rational is real does not justify restricting the test values to rationals. The already-declared reciprocal Archimedean result [L7] works for any real ε and can be used to prove the required real-ε statement directly.

Step 2.2 says the “other square is nonnegative”, while [F4] states only that a nonzero square is positive. If the other coefficient is zero, its square is zero, a case not established in the Fact or proof. Add the zero-square case (for example by citing multiplication by zero) before concluding a²+b²>0.

The definition sets |a+bi|=sqrt(a²+b²) and then invokes square-root existence, which applies to nonnegative radicands, but it does not establish a²+b²≥0 for arbitrary real a,b. A cited square-positivity result plus the zero case (or a direct ordered-field derivation) is needed to verify that the defined modulus exists for every complex number.

The proof uses [F5], which covers only nonzero squares, to assert (av-bu)²≥0 in step 1.3 and to infer in step 2.1 that a²+b²=0 forces a=b=0. The zero-square case is not stated or derived. A brief zero/nonzero case split, citing the field zero-product law and square-positivity result, is needed.

coverage_note: Reviewed both assigned pages, all ten assigned items, their cited direct sources needed for the claims, and the seven page prerequisites. No external web search was needed for these elementary/classical arguments. I did not reconstruct every transitive proof closure of every published supplier. Some dependent source sections (the sine-chord lemma before the logarithmic theorem, and the unit-interval Weierstrass/Bernstein suppliers before the closed-interval corollary) were opened after their consumers; I checked those suppliers before finalizing the findings, but did not strictly maintain supplier-first reading order. The three outside-batch current-run consumers of the Chebyshev definition were also opened; its original interface was retained.
